title: Jacob's ladder (Genesis 28:10–22)
hook: asleep on a stone, he dreams of angels going up and down
tomorrow: seven years like a few days

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was Esau, and his cry: bless me, even me also.

Jacob is alone on the road with nothing. Esau is furious, and says he'll kill his brother once their father dies, so Rebekah sends Jacob away, to her brother Laban in Haran. The quiet one who stayed in the tents now has no family, no flocks, no plan. The sun goes down. In the old JPS translation: "And he lighted upon the place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set." Not a town, not an inn: just the place where it got dark. He puts stones under his head and lies down. Anyone who has spent a night in an airport, a hospital waiting room or a strange bed knows that place. Nowhere. And there, he dreams.
screen: `RUNNING FROM ESAU.` → `HE LIGHTED UPON THE PLACE.` → `A STONE FOR A PILLOW.`

segments.voice: "And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it." Notice the order: ascending, then descending. You'd expect angels to come down from heaven first. Rashi, the medieval commentator, explains: the angels who had guarded Jacob in the land of Israel were going up, their shift over, and new angels, for the road ahead, were coming down. A changing of the guard over a sleeping man. Then God stands beside him and promises the land, children like the dust of the earth, and "I am with thee, and will keep thee whithersoever thou goest." Jacob wakes and says: "Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not." He was sure he was nowhere. He was at the gate of heaven. He names the spot Beth-el, the house of God. In later Hebrew, HaMakom, the Place, becomes one of the names for God. A midrash explains: God is the place of the world, and the world is not God's place. And the Talmud passage we met with Isaac says that Jacob, lighting on the place at nightfall, began the evening prayer. In that view, the set is complete: Abraham the morning, Isaac the afternoon, Jacob the night. Jacob lay down in the middle of nowhere, and woke up saying God had been there all along.
screen: `A LADDER FROM EARTH TO HEAVEN.` · `UP FIRST: A CHANGE OF GUARD.` · `I KNEW IT NOT.` · `HAMAKOM — THE PLACE.` · then, large: `SURELY THE LORD IS IN THIS PLACE.`

segments.voice: Notice exactly where you are right now, this room, this car, this bed, and rest your eyes on one ordinary thing in it: a wall, a cup, a patch of floor. If you pray, you can say Jacob's words silently: surely the LORD is in this place, and I knew it not; if not, just give this place your full attention, the way you would a place that mattered. You don't have to feel anything special.
Jacob's ladder: a dream on a stone, angels going up and down, and God standing beside him.
Your line: God was here all along. Even in the middle of nowhere. Day fifty-five, done.

screen: `DAY 55 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: SEVEN YEARS LIKE A FEW DAYS.`

howItsDone: Jews read Jacob's dream in the Torah portion Vayetze; tradition credits Jacob with the evening prayer, Maariv, and HaMakom, the Place, is used as a name for God, as in the words said to comfort mourners.

original.note: Hebrew: a ladder or stairway, set on the earth and reaching to heaven in Jacob's dream.

trapdoor: what you thought: a dream about a ladder to heaven.
what it means: a man on the run discovers that the middle of nowhere was the gate of heaven: God was here all along.
what a scholar hears: HaMakom, the Place, as a name for God (Genesis Rabbah 68:9), and Berakhot 26b reading vayifga bamakom as Jacob's evening prayer.

notes: Confirm JPS 1917 wording of Genesis 28:11, 28:12, 28:15 and 28:16.
The carry is lowercase 'god' in the index; the script's voice capitalizes God. Suggest capitalizing the index carry (owner-approved edit).
Rashi on 28:12: angels of the land ascend, angels outside the land descend. Confirm.
Genesis Rabbah 68:9: God is the place of the world, and the world is not His place. Confirm.
Sulam appears only here in the Hebrew Bible: confirm (hapax legomenon).
howItsDone: HaMakom in the mourners' comfort formula (HaMakom yenachem). Confirm.
